chunks: From him, from Faḍālah, from Kulayb al-Asadī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man, when he has a fracture, how he should perform the salat (prayer). He said: "If he fears for himself, then let him wipe over his splints and let him perform salat (prayer)."

key_terms.جَبَائِرِهِ: his splints or bandages placed over the injury
key_terms.كَسِيرًا: having a fracture or being physically broken/injured
key_terms.نَفْسِهِ: himself, meaning his bodily well-being or safety

ai.seo_question: How should a person with a fracture perform wudu (ablution) and salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who has a fracture and cannot perform normal washing due to fear of harm. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام instructs that such a person may wipe over the bandages or splints and still perform salat (prayer), showing facilitation in ritual purity and worship when injury is present.
